prompt: Compute the nth Fibonacci number iteratively, returning a long so large values fit. Complete the fibonacci method in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: An iterative Fibonacci keeps just two rolling values instead of recomputing the whole sequence, so it runs in linear time with constant memory. Each loop pass slides the pair forward: the old current becomes the new previous, and their sum becomes the new current. Using long matters because fib(50) = 12,586,269,025 does not fit in an int.
hints: Keep two variables, previous = 0 and current = 1, and loop n times.
In each pass compute next = previous + current, then shift previous = current and current = next.
After looping n times, previous holds fib(n). Make sure all three working variables are long, not int.
